item.title: Where the people come from
item.description:
A user block is the whole directory for a small site, or the service accounts a big one keeps out of its database. A site whose people are already in a database or in LDAP should not copy them into a second place that goes stale, so a users block reads them where they are. The users block is go-authn/directory’s hcldir, the same onego-fileshare reads: one directory is described the same way to both.

Written in the configuration 

user "alice" { password_file = "/etc/authnd/passwords/alice.pw" }

user "carol" {
 nt_hash = "…" # MD4(UTF16LE(password)), 32 hex
 authorized_keys = ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA… carol@laptop"] # published as sshPublicKey
}

group "staff" { members = ["alice", "carol"] }
field what it is
password the password, inline
password_file the same, read from a file (surrounding white space removed)
nt_hash MD4(UTF16LE(password)), 32 hex characters — for a site that holds that and not the password
totp_secret a base32 one-time-code secret, at least 128 bits; see a second factor
authorized_keys authorized_keys lines, published as sshPublicKey
authorized_keys_file the same, from a file
attributes from v0.11.0, what describes the person and proves nothing — sn, uidNumber, gidNumber, homeDirectory, mail… — as a map of strings or lists of strings; a group block takes it too. They decide what the entry is published as: see the entries

Refused at startup, naming the person:

  • password and password_file together — say which one;
  • password and nt_hash together — the hash is derived from the password,so two of them can disagree;
  • authorized_keys and authorized_keys_file together;
  • an nt_hash that is not 32 hex characters, an authorized_keys line that does not parse, a totp_secret under 128 bits;
  • the same user or group twice, and a group with no members.

A group member that no source knows is refused too, which is what catches a typo before it silently grants nothing:

$ authnd check cases/typo.hcl
authnd: group "staff" has "alise" in it, who is not in the configuration file

An nt_hash alone cannot bind

A person written with only nt_hash is published, can be handed to an SMB server through sambaNTPassword, and cannot bind to authnd itself: an LDAP simple bind sends the password, and an NT hash is not a way to check one here. bob below has only an NT hash, and the hash is that of the password sent:

$ ldapwhoami -x -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D uid=bob,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org -y bob.pwin
ldap_bind: Invalid credentials (49)

check says so, after the tables:

bob and eli cannot bind with a password: their sources hold only what an SMB server needs (an NT hash), which a bind cannot be checked against

Why it is refused, by design. An NT hash is MD4(UTF16LE(password)),unsalted and fast (MS-NLMP §3.3.1, NTOWFv1). Accepting it to check LDAP binds would widen what a leaked hash opens, from SMB to every application that binds through authnd. Kerberos refuses these people for a related reason: the NT hash is the RC4-HMAC key (RFC 4757 §2), and the realm issues AES only. This is a deliberate decision, not a missing feature, and there is no option to change it.

What to do instead. When migrating from a directory that holds only NT hashes (Samba, an exported AD), give each person a real password or a password check in their source: a password reset, or a users "ldap" source whose upstream directory checks the password itself. Do not keep the NT hash as the only credential.

In a SQL database 

users "sql" {
 driver = "postgres" # or mysql (mariadb), or sqlite
 dsn_file = "/etc/authnd/pg.dsn" # required: a DSN may hold a password
 users = "select login, secret, nt_hash from staff" # required
 groups = "select team, member from team_members" # optional
}

The queries are yours, because a site’s people are already in that site’s shape. The users query’s columns are read by position: a name,then any of a password, an NT hash, SSH keys (one per line) and a one-time-code secret, in that order — up to five columns. A NULL is a credential that person does not have. A password column is compared as it is stored: authnd has no setting for a hashed column. The groups query returns a group name and a member, one row per membership.

Two more queries, optional, read attributes by column alias rather than by position: users_attributes (a name, then one column per attribute) andgroups_attributes (a group, then the same). An unquoted alias is lower-cased by PostgreSQL. See the entries.

driver accepts postgres (or postgresql, pgx), mysql (or mariadb)and sqlite (or sqlite3). The database is reached at startup, before anything listens, so one that is not answering stops the server where somebody is watching:

$ authnd check cases/nodb
authnd: users "sql": the postgres database is not answering: failed to connect to `user=authnd database=authnd`:
127.0.0.1:1 (127.0.0.1): dial error: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused
127.0.0.1:1 (127.0.0.1): dial error: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused

PostgreSQL on the same machine through its socket and peer authentication needs no password in the DSN: host=/run/postgresql dbname=authnd user=authnd.SQLite in the state directory: file:/var/lib/authnd/people.db.

A key that belongs to the other kind of block is refused rather than ignored:

$ authnd check cases/sqlwrongkey.hcl
authnd: users "sql" has base_dn in it, which belongs to an ldap block

In another LDAP directory 

users "ldap" {
 url = "ldaps://ldap.example.org"
 base_dn = "ou=people,dc=example,dc=org"
 bind_dn = "cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org"
 bind_password_file = "/etc/authnd/upstream.pw"
}

url and base_dn are required. Where the people and groups are, and which attributes name them:

key default
user_filter (|(objectClass=posixAccount)(objectClass=account)(objectClass=uidObject))
user_attribute uid
group_base_dn base_dn
group_filter (|(objectClass=posixGroup)(objectClass=groupOfNames))
group_attribute cn
group_member_attribute none: memberUid (names) and member (DNs); set, it is the one attribute read
totp_attribute none: there is no standard attribute, and a guess would read nothing while looking like it had looked
attributes, group_attributes none: the attributes to copy from each person’s entry and each group’s, such as ["mail", "uidNumber", "homeDirectory"] and ["gidNumber"] (the entries)
start_tls false

A member DN counts only when it is the DN of an entry the people search returned: a DN outside them, or naming nobody, maps to nobody, and the name is never read out of the DN. sambaNTPassword and sshPublicKey are read under those names.

From v0.11.0 the defaults read more of an institution’s directory

The block is go-authn/directory’s, and directory v0.14.0, which authnd v0.11.0 embeds, widened its defaults: up to v0.10.2, user_filter was(objectClass=posixAccount), group_filter (objectClass=posixGroup) andgroup_member_attribute memberUid. A directory holding account oruidObject entries that are not posixAccounts — service accounts, hosts named by uid, people imported from elsewhere — now gives them to authnd, and each can be checked by a bind; its groupOfNames groups become groups here.To keep exactly the old set, write the old values:

users "ldap" {
 # ...
 user_filter = "(objectClass=posixAccount)"
 group_filter = "(objectClass=posixGroup)"
 group_member_attribute = "memberUid"
}

Two things are refused before anything is opened:

$ authnd check cases/ldap-clear.hcl
authnd: users "ldap" would send every password to "ldap.example.org" in the clear: use ldaps://, or start_tls = true (RFC 4513 §5.1.3)
$ authnd check cases/ldap-cred.hcl
authnd: users "ldap" has credentials in its url, and a url is printed: use bind_dn with bind_password_file

ldap:// to a loopback address and ldapi:// are accepted: nobody is on the way.

A directory behind this one checks passwords by binding to it; it does not hand them over. Here one authnd fronts another, under a different base;the one behind is the check example, served on 3893:

listen = "127.0.0.1:3894"
base_dn = "dc=example,dc=net"

users "ldap" {
 url = "ldap://127.0.0.1:3893"
 base_dn = "ou=people,dc=example,dc=org"
 group_base_dn = "ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org"
 bind_dn = "cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org"
 bind_password_file = "etc/authnd/reader.pw"
}

user "svc-backup" { password_file = "etc/authnd/svc-backup.pw" }
$ authnd check front2
ldap://127.0.0.1:3894, base dc=example,dc=net
USER FROM CAN PROVE PUBLISHED AS WITH
alice ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 a password check account, uidObject uid
bob ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 a password check account, uidObject uid
dora ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 a password check account, uidObject uid
eli ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 a password check account, uidObject uid
svc-backup the configuration file a password account, uidObject uid
GROUP MEMBERS PUBLISHED AS
engineers dora and eli groupOfNames
staff alice, bob and dora groupOfNames
alice has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
bob has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
dora has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
eli has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
svc-backup has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
group engineers has no gidNumber: not a posixGroup, published as a groupOfNames (member DNs, no memberUid)
group staff has no gidNumber: not a posixGroup, published as a groupOfNames (member DNs, no memberUid)
a bind carries a password
no reader is declared: nothing may search, and binds are not affected
sambaNTPassword is not published, so nothing here can authenticate an SMB session (NTLMv2 needs the password or its MD4, and a bind cannot answer it)
this configuration can be served

Every person the directory behind publishes is an account and every group a groupOfNames, since none has POSIX attributes: the defaults read them,and the groups’ member DNs map to the people imported. With the defaults up to v0.10.2, (objectClass=posixAccount) would have matched none of them.

A password check is enough for a bind, and is never enough for aKerberos ticket or for SMB.

Order, and the one exception

Sources are asked in the order they are written, and the first one that knows a name owns it. The user blocks always come first, so a service account written down locally is not overridden by somebody with the same name in the database. Group membership is the union of every source: a group that a group block and a database’s groups query both name has the members of both.

Two names that differ only by case are refused

A uid is compared ignoring case (RFC 4519 §2.39), and so is every DN, soDora in the file and dora in a database are one name to LDAP and two people to anything that compares bytes — a password change by one would land on the other. Such a configuration does not start:

$ authnd check cases/case.hcl
authnd: "Dora" (from the configuration file) and "dora" (from a sqlite database) differ only by case, and an LDAP name does not tell them apart: a uid is compared ignoring case. Rename one of them

Read once

Every source is read once, at startup. A person added to the database, or a membership changed in the directory behind this one, is served after a restart, not before. That includes a password column in a database: it is read with the rest of the row. A directory behind this one is different only in that a bind is checked by binding to it, so a password changed there is the one that works. The other exception is a password a person changes through authnd itself, which is applied at once.There is no reload; see running it.

item.title: The entries authnd publishes, and the schema it serves
item.description:
Every entry authnd publishes passes the schema it serves. From v0.11.0 each person and group is a standard-schema entry, built from what its source gave, and checked with go-authn/ldap’s schema.Validate against the schema a client can read at cn=Subschema before it is ever returned by a search. A client that reads the schema and believes it — an LDAP browser, a synchronisation tool, a directory replicating this one — is shown what it was told. Up to v0.10.2 every person was top, person, posixAccount with none of the attributes those classes require, and sambaNTPassword sat on an entry with no class that allows it.

A consumer filtering on posixAccount or posixGroup sees fewer entries

A person without uidNumber, gidNumber and homeDirectory is no longer aposixAccount, and a group without a gidNumber is no longer aposixGroup. A program that searches (objectClass=posixAccount) or(objectClass=posixGroup) no longer finds them. That includes go-authn/directory’s ldapdir up to v0.13.0, and so go-fileshare until it requires directory v0.14.0, whose defaults also read account, uidObject and groupOfNames (directory).Give people and groups those attributes, or point the consumer at(objectClass=uidObject), which every person carries.

The shapes

Every superclass is listed, as RFC 4512 §3.3 asks.

a person with… objectClass cn
no sn top, account (RFC 4524 §3.1) only when another class allows it
sn top, person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson (RFC 4519, RFC 2798) yes
… and uidNumber, gidNumber, homeDirectory, all three + posixAccount (RFC 2307) yes
… and SSH keys + ldapPublicKey (openssh-lpk), with sshPublicKey
… and a published NT hash with a sambaSID + sambaSamAccount (Samba), with sambaSID and sambaNTPassword: see the samba block allowed
… always + uidObject (RFC 4519 §3.14), so (objectClass=uidObject) finds everybody
a group with… objectClass members
a gidNumber top, posixGroup (RFC 2307) memberUid, names
no gidNumber, somebody in it top, groupOfNames (RFC 4519 §3.5) member, the DNs this server publishes
no gidNumber, nobody in it top, organizationalRole (RFC 4519 §3.10) none
a gidNumber, nobody in it top, posixGroup none: an attribute has at least one value

uid is the person’s name, and so is cn wherever a class allows it. Anaccount alone does not allow cn (its MAY is description, seeAlso,l, o, ou and host), so a person without sn and without the POSIX trio carries uid and no cn.

Why these choices, from authnd’s own reasons:

  • posixGroup follows RFC 2307, not draft-howard-rfc2307bis-02. The draft makes posixGroup AUXILIARY and expired unpublished; an AUXILIARYposixGroup would need a structural class beside it, groupOfNames, whosemember an empty group cannot give.
  • organizationalRole for an empty group without a gidNumber. groupOfNames and groupOfUniqueNames both require a member, and the ways of inventing one are false: member: "" names the root DSE, and the group’s own DN makes it a member of itself. organizationalRole is the one standard structural class whose only MUST is cn, and it takesdescription, ou and seeAlso as groupOfNames does.
  • Auxiliary classes without DIT content rules. RFC 4512 §2.4.3 forbids auxiliary classes on an entry whose structural class has no DIT content rule. Every directory server in use allows them, and so does Validate.

Adding attributes

What a source says about somebody that proves nothing — a uidNumber, a home directory, a mail address — is an attribute, published as given.They are go-authn/directory’s attributes,from v0.13.0, and they are kept apart from credentials: a name that holds a secret, or one the server derives itself, is refused before anything is read.

In a user or group block 

user "dora" {
 password_file = "/etc/authnd/passwords/dora.pw"
 authorized_keys = ["ssh-ed25519 AAAA… dora@laptop"]
 attributes = {
 sn = "Explorer" # inetOrgPerson
 uidNumber = "1000" # the three: posixAccount
 gidNumber = "1000"
 homeDirectory = "/home/dora"
 mail = ["dora@example.org", "d.explorer@example.org"]
 }
}

group "engineers" {
 members = ["dora", "eli"]
 attributes = { gidNumber = "2000" } # a posixGroup; without it, a groupOfNames
}

A value is a string or a list of strings; null leaves the attribute out.A number is refused, because an LDAP value is a string and authnd does not choose how a number is spelled:

$ authnd check cases/number.hcl
authnd: user "alice": attributes: uidNumber is the number 1000: write it as a string, "1000" -- an LDAP value is a string, and this does not choose how a number is spelled
$ authnd check cases/secret.hcl
authnd: user "alice": attributes: directory: not an attribute this package carries: "userPassword" holds a secret, and attributes are published: a credential has its own option or none

Refused the same way, whatever their case: any name holding a secret(userPassword, sambaNTPassword, unicodePwd, krbPrincipalKey and the rest of go-authn/directory’s list, or any name containing password,passwd, pwd, secret, credential, hash or privatekey);sshPublicKey, which has authorized_keys; uid, cn and objectClass,which the server derives; member, memberUid and the other membership attributes, which members answers; the operational attributes a server maintains; and a name in numeric form (2.5.4.35 is userPassword).

In a SQL database

Two optional queries of a users "sql" block read attributes by column alias. The first column is the person’s or the group’s name; every other column is an attribute named by its alias:

users "sql" {
 driver = "sqlite"
 dsn_file = "/etc/authnd/people.dsn"
 users = "select login, secret, null, ssh_keys from staff"
 groups = "select team, member from teams"
 users_attributes = "select login, sn, uid as uidNumber, gid as gidNumber, home as homeDirectory, mail from person_attrs"
 groups_attributes = "select team, gid as gidNumber, description from team_attrs"
}
  • The positional users and groups queries are unchanged, and a sixth positional column is still refused: attributes come by name, in their own query.
  • A column whose alias is not an attribute description (an unaliased expression such as count(*)), or names a credential, is refused with its column number before a row is read.
  • NULL and '' are absent. A name may come back on several rows, and the values of all of them are kept, so a join to a table of addresses gives a person several.
  • A group named only in groups_attributes exists, with nobody in it:that is how a person’s own primary group is written.

The case of an alias is the database’s

PostgreSQL folds an unquoted alias to lower case: as uidNumber comes back as uidnumber. Attribute names are case-insensitive, so it is the same attribute and the entry is the same entry to every LDAP client, but the spelling authnd prints is the database’s. Quote the alias where the spelling matters: gid as "gidNumber". SQLite keeps an alias as written.

From another LDAP directory

A users "ldap" block copies the attributes it is told to, from each person’s entry and each group’s: attributes = ["mail", "uidNumber", "homeDirectory"] and group_attributes = ["gidNumber"]. Seepeople.

A configuration, and what it publishes

The SQL block above, with a reader, over a SQLite database of five people and four groups, as the v0.11.0 release binary checks it:

listen = "127.0.0.1:3893"
base_dn = "dc=example,dc=org"

reader "cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org" { password_file = "etc/authnd/reader.pw" }

users "sql" {
 driver = "sqlite"
 dsn_file = "etc/authnd/people.dsn"
 users = "select login, secret, null, ssh_keys from staff"
 groups = "select team, member from teams"
 users_attributes = "select login, sn, uid as uidNumber, gid as gidNumber, home as homeDirectory, mail from person_attrs"
 groups_attributes = "select team, gid as gidNumber, description from team_attrs"
}
$ authnd check etc/authnd
ldap://127.0.0.1:3893, base dc=example,dc=org
USER FROM CAN PROVE PUBLISHED AS WITH
dora a sqlite database a password and 1 key person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson, posixAccount, ldapPublicKey, uidObject uid, cn, sn, uidNumber, gidNumber, homeDirectory, mail and sshPublicKey
eli a sqlite database a password account, posixAccount, uidObject uid, cn, uidNumber, gidNumber and homeDirectory
fay a sqlite database a password person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson, uidObject uid, cn, sn and mail
gus a sqlite database a password account, uidObject uid
hal a sqlite database a password account, uidObject uid
GROUP MEMBERS PUBLISHED AS
alumni nobody organizationalRole
engineers dora and eli posixGroup
nobody-yet nobody posixGroup
readers fay and gus groupOfNames
fay has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as person, organizationalPerson, inetOrgPerson, uidObject
gus has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
hal has no homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
hal is published without uidNumber: no class of the entry allows it; posixAccount would
hal is published without gidNumber: no class of the entry allows it; posixAccount and posixGroup would
hal is published without mail: no class of the entry allows it; inetOrgPerson would
group alumni has no gidNumber and nobody in it: not a posixGroup, published as an organizationalRole (a groupOfNames needs a member)
group readers has no gidNumber: not a posixGroup, published as a groupOfNames (member DNs, no memberUid)
a bind carries a password
cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org may search; every other bound client may not
sambaNTPassword is not published, so nothing here can authenticate an SMB session (NTLMv2 needs the password or its MD4, and a bind cannot answer it)
this configuration can be served

PUBLISHED AS is each entry’s object classes, without top, and WITH its attributes, read off the entries a search returns. hal has a uidNumber, agidNumber and a mail and no homeDirectory or sn: hal is an account,which allows none of the three, so they are dropped and the rest is published. The server says the same at startup (and stopping when it was stopped):

$ authnd --config etc/authnd
ldap on 127.0.0.1:3893, serving 5 people from a sqlite database
uid=hal,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org is published without uidNumber: no class of the entry allows it; posixAccount would
uid=hal,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org is published without gidNumber: no class of the entry allows it; posixAccount and posixGroup would
uid=hal,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org is published without mail: no class of the entry allows it; inetOrgPerson would
stopping

Read back by OpenLDAP’s ldapsearch, with the reader’s password in a file:

$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -o ldif-wrap=no -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b ou=people,dc=example,dc=org '(|(uid=dora)(uid=eli)(uid=gus)(uid=hal))'
dn: uid=dora,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: person
objectClass: organizationalPerson
objectClass: inetOrgPerson
objectClass: posixAccount
objectClass: ldapPublicKey
objectClass: uidObject
uid: dora
cn: dora
sn: Explorer
uidNumber: 1000
gidNumber: 1000
homeDirectory: /home/dora
mail: dora@example.org
sshPublicKey: ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKTfVR7FqXWE/0VEcjrUhK+Fz/MLqlwGPIxalr6onRMn dora@laptop
dn: uid=eli,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: account
objectClass: posixAccount
objectClass: uidObject
uid: eli
cn: eli
uidNumber: 1001
gidNumber: 1001
homeDirectory: /home/eli
dn: uid=gus,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: account
objectClass: uidObject
uid: gus
dn: uid=hal,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: account
objectClass: uidObject
uid: hal
$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org '(objectClass=*)'
dn: cn=alumni,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: organizationalRole
cn: alumni
description: people who were here
dn: cn=engineers,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: posixGroup
cn: engineers
gidNumber: 2000
memberUid: dora
memberUid: eli
dn: cn=nobody-yet,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: posixGroup
cn: nobody-yet
gidNumber: 2001
dn: cn=readers,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=org
objectClass: top
objectClass: groupOfNames
cn: readers
description: people who read
member: uid=fay,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
member: uid=gus,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org

alumni is named only in groups_attributes, so it exists with nobody in it; without a gidNumber it is an organizationalRole. nobody-yet has agidNumber and nobody, so it is a posixGroup without memberUid.

Which class finds whom:

$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b dc=example,dc=org '(objectClass=uidObject)' 1.1
dn: uid=dora,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
dn: uid=eli,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
dn: uid=fay,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
dn: uid=gus,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
dn: uid=hal,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b dc=example,dc=org '(objectClass=posixAccount)' 1.1
dn: uid=dora,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
dn: uid=eli,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org

What is dropped, and what is withheld

given the entry why
uidNumber, gidNumber, no homeDirectory, no sn account, uidObject, without the two no class of the entry allows it; posixAccount would
mail, no sn account, uidObject, without it no class of the entry allows it; inetOrgPerson would
a type the schema does not define the rest the schema served here does not define it
mail on a group without a gidNumber groupOfNames, without it
two homeDirectory values with the POSIX trio withheld: SINGLE-VALUE, nothing to drop
a gidNumber that is not an integer withheld: not of its syntax

Only what a source gave is dropped, and which attribute is not allowed is Validate’s answer, not a second reading of the schema. The entry is validated again after dropping. An entry that still fails is withheld:it is absent from every search, the startup log names it, and check lists it with every problem Validate found. An attribute authnd derives itself(uid, cn, objectClass, sshPublicKey, sambaSID, sambaNTPassword)that the schema refused would be a defect in authnd, and withholds the entry rather than publish it without.

alice’s gidNumber is a word here:

listen = "127.0.0.1:3893"
base_dn = "dc=example,dc=org"

reader "cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org" { password_file = "etc/authnd/reader.pw" }

user "alice" {
 password_file = "etc/authnd/alice.pw"
 attributes = {
 uidNumber = "1000"
 gidNumber = "staff"
 homeDirectory = "/home/alice"
 }
}

user "bob" { password_file = "etc/authnd/bob.pw" }
$ authnd check cases/withheld.hcl
ldap://127.0.0.1:3893, base dc=example,dc=org
USER FROM CAN PROVE PUBLISHED AS WITH
alice the configuration file a password NOT PUBLISHED (see below) uid, cn, gidNumber, homeDirectory and uidNumber
bob the configuration file a password account, uidObject uid
bob has no uidNumber, gidNumber or homeDirectory: not a posixAccount, published as account, uidObject
alice is NOT published: as account, posixAccount, uidObject it fails the schema:
- the value "staff" of gidNumber is not of its syntax 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.27
a bind carries a password
cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org may search; every other bound client may not
sambaNTPassword is not published, so nothing here can authenticate an SMB session (NTLMv2 needs the password or its MD4, and a bind cannot answer it)
this configuration can be served

Served, alice can still bind and is in no search, and the server says why at startup:

$ authnd --config cases/withheld.hcl
ldap on 127.0.0.1:3893, serving 2 people from the configuration file
uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org is NOT published: it fails the schema: the value "staff" of gidNumber is not of its syntax 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.27
$ ldapwhoami -x -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org -y alice.pwin
dn:uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b dc=example,dc=org '(uid=alice)'

What is withheld is the entry a search returns, not the identity.

The schema it serves

The root DSE names it (subschemaSubentry: cn=Subschema, onthe root DSE),and a base search of cn=Subschema returns it (RFC 4512 §4.2): the standard definitions go-authn/ldap embeds — RFC 4512, 4517, 4519, 4523,4524, 2798, 2307, 3672 and 3045, and openssh-lpk — plus Samba’ssambaSamAccount, sambaSID and sambaNTPassword when there is asamba block. The definitions are published only when asked for by name or with +. Trimmed where marked:

$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -o ldif-wrap=no -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -s base -b cn=Subschema '+' '*'
dn: cn=Subschema
objectClass: top
objectClass: subentry
objectClass: subschema
cn: Subschema
subtreeSpecification: {}
ldapSyntaxes: ( 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.3 DESC 'Attribute Type Description' )
[...]
matchingRules: ( 2.5.13.15 NAME 'integerOrderingMatch' SYNTAX 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.27 )
[...]
attributeTypes: ( 1.3.6.1.1.1.1.0 NAME 'uidNumber' DESC 'An integer uniquely identifying a user in an administrative domain' EQUALITY integerMatch ORDERING integerOrderingMatch SYNTAX 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.27 SINGLE-VALUE )
attributeTypes: ( 1.3.6.1.1.1.1.1 NAME 'gidNumber' DESC 'An integer uniquely identifying a group in an administrative domain' EQUALITY integerMatch ORDERING integerOrderingMatch SYNTAX 1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.115.121.1.27 SINGLE-VALUE )
[...]
objectClasses: ( 2.5.6.9 NAME 'groupOfNames' SUP top STRUCTURAL MUST ( member $ cn ) MAY ( businessCategory $ seeAlso $ owner $ ou $ o $ description ) )
[...]
objectClasses: ( 1.3.6.1.1.3.1 NAME 'uidObject' SUP top AUXILIARY MUST uid )
objectClasses: ( 0.9.2342.19200300.100.4.5 NAME 'account' SUP top STRUCTURAL MUST uid MAY ( description $ seeAlso $ l $ o $ ou $ host ) )
[...]
objectClasses: ( 1.3.6.1.1.1.2.0 NAME 'posixAccount' DESC 'Abstraction of an account with POSIX attributes' SUP top AUXILIARY MUST ( cn $ uid $ uidNumber $ gidNumber $ homeDirectory ) MAY ( userPassword $ loginShell $ gecos $ description ) )
[...]
objectClasses: ( 1.3.6.1.1.1.2.2 NAME 'posixGroup' DESC 'Abstraction of a group of accounts' SUP top STRUCTURAL MUST ( cn $ gidNumber ) MAY ( userPassword $ memberUid $ description ) )
[...]

The whole entry was 327 lines: 49 syntaxes, 40 matching rules, 36 matching rule uses, 143 attribute types and 52 object classes. Unlike a search under the base, the subschema entry, like the root DSE, is answered to an anonymous client: the same query without -D and -y returned it.

Filters use the schema’s matching rules, so (uidNumber>=1000) compares integers. uidNumber and gidNumber have ORDERING integerOrderingMatch, which RFC 2307 does not give them; slapd and draft-howard-rfc2307bis-02 do, and so does go-authn/ldap(its one departure).As strings, 1000 sorts before 999:

$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b dc=example,dc=org '(uidNumber>=1000)' uidNumber
dn: uid=dora,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
uidNumber: 1000
dn: uid=eli,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
uidNumber: 1001
$ ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://127.0.0.1:3893 -D cn=reader,dc=example,dc=org -y reader.pwin -b dc=example,dc=org '(uidNumber>=999)' uidNumber
dn: uid=dora,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
uidNumber: 1000
dn: uid=eli,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org
uidNumber: 1001

hal is not there: hal’s uidNumber was dropped. A range on an attribute with no ORDERING rule, such as uid, is Undefined and matches nothing.

item.title: directory — who somebody is, and what proves them
item.description:
Who is somebody, and what can prove them? One model over a list held in memory, a SQL database, an LDAP server, or user and group blocks in a configuration file — and the point of it is the second half of the question.

go get github.com/go-authn/directory@v0.14.0

What proves somebody is not one thing

It is a fact about protocols. NTLMv2 (SMB) is a challenge-response: the client never sends the password, so the server must hold the password orMD4(UTF16LE(password)) — the NT hash — and an LDAP bind cannot authenticate an SMB session. A KDC must decrypt with the person’s key, so only a source holding the password can back a realm. SSH needs a public key.A second factor needs the secret behind the six digits.

So an Identity says which Credentials its source gave — Password,NTHash, Verifier (a hash comparison or a bind), PublicKeys,TOTPSecret — and Identity.Can lets a server say you can use WebDAV and not SMB before somebody meets a refusal at a mount. Each protocol has its own method:

answers from
Verify(password) anything handed the password the source’s verifier first (it may be an LDAP bind), else the held password, compared in constant time on SHA-256 digests so not even the length leaks
NTKey() NTLMv2 the published hash, or derived from the password; ErrNoCredential with neither
Derive(f), KerberosKey(f) a KDC, AWS SigV4 — anything that must possess the secret the password only; the derivation is the caller’s function
Keys() SSH authorized_keys lines
TOTPSecret() totp a column, or an LDAP attribute the caller names

The sources

package reads imports
directory a Static list, and a Set of sources in order the standard library only
directory/sqldir any *sql.DB, with your queries no driver: the program picks one
directory/ldapdir an LDAP server go-ldap/ldap/v3
directory/hcldir a users block naming a database or an LDAP server, and user/group blocks holding people x/crypto/ssh, hashicorp/hcl/v2, zclconf/go-cty
directory/ldaptest an LDAP server to test against glauth/ldap

In a Set, the first source that knows a name owns it, so a service account written down locally need not be put in LDAP. Group membership is theunion of every source. Sources are read when a server starts; a password check may reach the source every time, because a bind cannot be cached without holding the secret.

hcldir does not decode HCL: the caller decodes the block and hands it over.It imports HCL only to write, for SetPassword. The build tags nosql andnoldap leave a kind out of hcldir entirely.

Example 

package main

import (
 "errors"
 "fmt"

 "github.com/go-authn/directory"
)

func main() {
 local := &directory.Static{
 Name: "the configuration file",
 People: []*directory.Identity{
 directory.NewIdentity("dora", directory.WithPassword("hunter2")),
 directory.NewIdentity("eli", directory.WithVerifier(func(pw string) error {
 return directory.ErrWrongPassword // a bind against somebody else's LDAP, say
 })),
 directory.NewIdentity("svc-backup", directory.WithPublicKeys("ssh-ed25519 AAAA...elided... backup")),
 },
 Groups: map[string][]string{"staff": {"dora", "eli"}, "nobody": {}},
 }
 people := directory.NewSet(local) // more sources after it: sqldir, ldapdir...

 ids, _ := people.Identities()
 for _, id := range ids {
 fmt.Println(id.Name(), "password:", id.Can(directory.Password), "verifier:", id.Can(directory.Verifier),
 "keys:", id.Can(directory.PublicKeys), "from", id.Where())
 }

 // NTLMv2 needs MD4(UTF16LE(password)): dora's can be derived, eli's cannot.
 for _, id := range ids[:2] {
 _, err := id.NTKey()
 fmt.Println(id.Name(), "SMB:", err == nil, errors.Is(err, directory.ErrNoCredential))
 }

 // An empty group is an empty answer; a group nobody has is an error.
 fmt.Println(people.Members("nobody"))
 fmt.Println(people.Members("admins"))

 // @group is expanded; an empty group, or one nobody has, is refused.
 fmt.Println(directory.Expand([]string{"@staff", "svc-backup"}, people))
 fmt.Println(directory.Expand([]string{"@nobody"}, local))
 _, err := directory.Expand([]string{"@nobody"}, people)
 fmt.Println(err, errors.Is(err, directory.ErrEmptyGroup), errors.Is(err, directory.ErrNoSuchGroup))
 _, err = directory.Expand([]string{"@admins"}, people)
 fmt.Println(err, errors.Is(err, directory.ErrEmptyGroup), errors.Is(err, directory.ErrNoSuchGroup))
}
dora password: true verifier: true keys: false from the configuration file
eli password: false verifier: true keys: false from the configuration file
svc-backup password: false verifier: false keys: true from the configuration file
dora SMB: true false
eli SMB: false true
[] <nil>
[] directory: no such group: "admins", in the configuration file
[dora eli svc-backup] <nil>
[] directory: the group has no members: "nobody": nobody would be allowed
directory: the group has no members: "nobody": nobody would be allowed true false
directory: no such group: "admins", in the configuration file false true

A held password also answers Can(Verifier): it can be compared.

An empty group is a group: Members answers it, Expand refuses it

From v0.12.0, Set.Members returns an empty list and no error for a group a source has with nobody in it, so a server that lists groups can publish it.Expand still refuses it, with ErrEmptyGroup, which is notErrNoSuchGroup: a group nobody has is a typo or a deleted group, an empty one is a group to fill. A caller that tolerates a group granting nothing tests for both. In v0.11.x, Set.Members returned ErrNoSuchGroup for an empty group, and Expand of @nobody through the Set printed[] directory: no such group: "nobody".

Attributes

From v0.13.0 an Identity can carry attributes: what a source says about somebody that proves nothing — a uidNumber, a home directory, a mail address. They are kept apart from credentials on purpose: a credential decides who may log in, an attribute is published to everybody allowed to search. A server such as authnd turns them into the attributes of an LDAP entry, and its schema decides what the entry is.

package main

import (
 "errors"
 "fmt"

 "github.com/go-authn/directory"
)

func main() {
 a, err := directory.NewAttributes(
 directory.Attribute{Name: "uidNumber", Values: []string{"1000"}},
 directory.Attribute{Name: "mail", Values: []string{"dora@example.org"}},
 directory.Attribute{Name: "MAIL", Values: []string{"d.explorer@example.org", "dora@example.org"}},
 )
 fmt.Println(err)
 dora := directory.NewIdentity("dora", directory.WithPassword("hunter2"), directory.WithAttributes(a))
 fmt.Println(dora.Attributes().Names(), dora.Attributes().Get("UIDNUMBER"), dora.Attributes().Get("mail"))

 // What is published cannot hold a secret, nor what a server derives or answers itself.
 for _, name := range []string{"userPassword", "sambaNTPassword", "radiusHash", "cn", "memberUid", "2.5.4.35"} {
 _, err := directory.NewAttributes(directory.Attribute{Name: name, Values: []string{"x"}})
 fmt.Println(errors.Is(err, directory.ErrAttributeName), err)
 }
}
<nil>
[uidNumber mail] [1000] [dora@example.org d.explorer@example.org]
true directory: not an attribute this package carries: "userPassword" holds a secret, and attributes are published: a credential has its own option or none
true directory: not an attribute this package carries: "sambaNTPassword" holds a secret, and attributes are published: a credential has its own option or none
true directory: not an attribute this package carries: "radiusHash" looks like it holds a secret (its name contains "hash"), and attributes are published: a credential has its own option or none
true directory: not an attribute this package carries: "cn" is derived by the server from the name it publishes the entry under
true directory: not an attribute this package carries: "memberUid" is membership, which Members answers: a second answer would disagree with it
true directory: not an attribute this package carries: "2.5.4.35" is an OID: name it by its descriptor, so that what is refused by name stays refused

Names are RFC 4512 attribute descriptions, compared ignoring case and the order of options, so mail and MAIL are one attribute, spelled the first way it was given; an exact repeat of a value is kept once. Values are strings and are not interpreted: "1000" is a uidNumber because a server’s schema says so. An empty value, or none, is refused.

refused why
56 named secrets — userPassword, authPassword, userPKCS12, sambaNTPassword, sambaLMPassword, unicodePwd, krbPrincipalKey, krb5Key, ipaNTHash, ipatokenOTPkey, oathSecret, olcRootPW, … read off RFC 4519, RFC 3112, RFC 2798 and the Samba, Active Directory, MIT and Heimdal Kerberos, FreeIPA, 389-ds and OpenLDAP schemas
any name containing password, passwd, pwd, secret, credential, hash or privatekey a list only knows the schemas somebody read; the one standard name this would catch, secretary (RFC 4524), is allowed
sshPublicKey it has its own path, WithPublicKeys, so that Can(PublicKeys) stays true
uid, userid, cn, commonName, objectClass a server derives them from the name it publishes the entry under
member, uniqueMember, memberUid, memberOf membership is what Members answers, and a second answer would disagree
createTimestamp, modifyTimestamp, creatorsName, modifiersName, structuralObjectClass, governingStructureRule, subschemaSubentry, entryDN, entryUUID a server maintains them; a configuration could only forge them
a name in numeric form refusals are by name, and 2.5.4.35 is userPassword

ReservedAttributes() returns the whole list, 75 names with their reasons;CheckAttributeName applies the rule alone, so a configuration can be refused before anything is read.

Where they come from:

  • hcldir: attributes = { … } in user and group blocks, a string or a list of strings per name; a number is refused with the fix in the message (write it as a string, “1000”), and null leaves the attribute out.
  • sqldir: two optional queries, users_attributes andgroups_attributes (Queries.PeopleAttributes, GroupAttributes), readby column alias: the first column is the name, every other column an attribute named by its alias. A column whose alias is not an attribute description, or names a credential, is refused with its column number before a row is read. NULL and '' are absent, and several rows for one name add values. A group named only there exists, with nobody in it.⛔ PostgreSQL lower-cases an unquoted alias (as uidNumber comes backuidnumber): the same attribute, spelled the database’s way. Quote it,as "uidNumber", where the spelling matters.
  • ldapdir: Config.Attributes and GroupAttributes (attributes and group_attributes in a users "ldap" block) name what to copy from each person’s entry and each group’s, matched by RFC 4512 equivalence and kept in the configured spelling. Besides the list above, it refuses thetotp_attribute and the group’s naming and member attributes. A subtype the directory returns besides (description;lang-fr for description) is not copied: ask for it by name.

A group’s attributes come from Set.GroupAttributes, through the optionalGroupAttributer: the first source to give an attribute owns it, so agidNumber in a local file overrides the directory’s while a description only the directory has comes through, and a broken source is an error even when another answered. A person’s attributes come with the person, from the source that owns the name.

ldapdir’s defaults

setting (users "ldap" / ldapdir.Config) default from v0.14.0 up to v0.13.0
user_filter / UserFilter (|(objectClass=posixAccount)(objectClass=account)(objectClass=uidObject)), ldapdir.DefaultUserFilter (objectClass=posixAccount)
user_attribute / UserAttribute uid the same
group_base_dn / GroupBaseDN base_dn the same
group_filter / GroupFilter (|(objectClass=posixGroup)(objectClass=groupOfNames)), ldapdir.DefaultGroupFilter (objectClass=posixGroup)
group_attribute / GroupAttribute cn the same
group_member_attribute / MemberAttribute none: memberUid (names) and member (DNs); set, it is the one attribute read memberUid

The three classes are the standard ones that carry a uid: posixAccount (RFC 2307), account (RFC 4524 §3.1) and uidObject (RFC 4519 §3.14).go-authn/authnd from v0.11.0 publishes a person without the POSIX attributes as an account or an inetOrgPerson, puts uidObject on every person, and publishes a group without a gidNumber as a groupOfNames. Under the old defaults such people and groups were not read at all.

v0.14.0 widens what an institution’s directory gives

A directory holding account or uidObject entries that are not posixAccounts — service accounts, hosts named by uid, people imported from elsewhere — now gives them to every program that kept the default, and each of them can then be checked against the directory by a bind. ItsgroupOfNames groups become groups, and an @group rule naming one now grants what it says. A plain inetOrgPerson with none of the three classes is still not read. To keep exactly the old set:

users "ldap" {
 # ...
 user_filter = "(objectClass=posixAccount)"
 group_filter = "(objectClass=posixGroup)"
 group_member_attribute = "memberUid"
}

A member DN adds no person. It maps to somebody only when it is, by distinguishedNameMatch (RFC 4517 §4.2.15), the DN of an entry the people search returned. A DN outside those entries, or naming nobody, maps to nobody, and so does uid=alice,ou=elsewhere,… when alice was imported fromou=people. Up to v0.13.0 a DN in the member attribute was reduced to the value of its first RDN, whoever’s it was, so uid=alice,ou=elsewhere,…,cn=alice,… and uid=zed,… became members named alice, alice and zed.

ldaptest, the test directory, now applies base and filter to every search,gives each person an objectClass (Person.ObjectClasses, by defaulttop, account, posixAccount) and has groupOfNames groups(GroupsOfNames), so a test of a client’s filters can fail.

What it refuses, and why

  • A group with nobody in it, and a group no source has, when Expand turns @group into people — errors, not empty lists: a configuration that grants nothing to nobody reads exactly like one that works. The first isErrEmptyGroup, the second ErrNoSuchGroup, and errors.Is tells them apart. Set.Members answers an empty group with an empty list; a group no source has is ErrNoSuchGroup there too. A source that is broken is reported apart from one that lacks the group, and wins over an empty answer.
  • An LDAP directory reached in the clear. A simple bind carries the password itself (RFC 4513), so ldapdir.New and a users "ldap" block refuse ldap:// to another machine unless StartTLS is set. ldaps://,ldapi:// and ldap:// to a loopback address are accepted. There is no switch to turn this off.
  • An empty password at an LDAP bind. In LDAP it is an unauthenticated bind, which most directories answer with success; ldapdir answersErrWrongPassword without dialling.
  • Any other failed bind taken for a wrong password. Only LDAP result 49,invalidCredentials, is ErrWrongPassword. A connection dropped during the bind, a directory answering busy (51) or unavailable (52), is returned asldapdir: the directory did not answer the bind: …, wrapping the LDAP error.The password is refused either way; what changes is that a server’s log no longer says wrong password to somebody who typed it right. Before v0.11.2 every failed bind was ErrWrongPassword.
  • Credentials in an LDAP URL — a URL is printed; BindDN andBindPassword are fields.
  • An NT hash that is not 16 bytes (ParseNTHash), rather than padding it into a hash that fails every login as a wrong password.
  • Derive or KerberosKey for an identity without the password. A verifier’s yes is not a key.
  • An attribute that is a secret, or that a server answers itself —the list above — wherever it is configured: in a block, as a SQL alias, or in ldapdir’s list to copy.

The NT hash and the TOTP secret are credentials, not hashes of one

Whoever holds sambaNTPassword authenticates as that person exactly as if they held the password; whoever holds a TOTP secret produces every future code. WithVerifier’s error goes to the server, never to the client.

What it is checked against

  • OpenLDAP’s ldapsearch reads ldaptest’s directory — the entries, thesambaNTPassword of the one person who has it, the group — and is refused with Invalid credentials (49) for a wrong password. The CI’s Linux lanes install ldap-utils; where ldapsearch is absent the test skips, as nothing in this module’s CI turns that skip into a failure.
  • ldapdir against glauth/ldap, an independent LDAP server, not a fake;the fixture allows the unauthenticated bind, so the test fails if ldapdir stops refusing it first.
  • sqldir against a real SQLite database through a real driver. The attributes queries were also run once by hand against PostgreSQL 18.6 through pgx, not in CI: an unquoted alias came back lower-cased and was found anyway, a quoted one kept its case, and an alias naminguserPassword was refused.
  • ldapdir’s filters against ldaptest, which from v0.14.0 applies them:the default user filter leaves out a plain inetOrgPerson (TestTheDefaultUserFilter), and the group filter adds no identity(TestTheGroupFilterAddsNoIdentity).
  • MD4 against RFC 1320’s test vectors.

The coverage lane fails below 85% (its stated standard is 100%), and thenosql and noldap builds are checked in CI.

Reference

pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-authn/directory@v0.14.0
